questions.q: What actually runs a mapping data flow's transformation logic?
options: A managed, scaled-out Apache Spark cluster
The Azure portal directly, with no compute involved
A self-hosted integration runtime, always
SQL Server's own query engine
questions.explain: You design the transformation visually; Data Factory translates it into Spark code and runs it on a managed Spark cluster you never provision yourself.

questions.q: What are the three parts of the data flow authoring canvas?
options: Top bar, graph, and configuration panel
Source, Sink, and Trigger
Author, Monitor, and Manage
Pipeline, Dataset, and Linked Service
questions.explain: The top bar holds validation and debug controls, the graph shows the actual transformation stream, and the configuration panel shows settings for whatever's selected.

questions.q: Do you need debug mode turned on to view the Inspect tab?
options: No — Inspect shows read-only metadata without an active debug session
Yes, Inspect requires an active Spark cluster
Inspect only works after a data flow has been published
Inspect and Data Preview are the exact same feature
questions.explain: Inspect shows column metadata (names, types, what changed) without needing debug mode — unlike Data Preview, which needs an active debug cluster.

questions.q: What activity actually runs a mapping data flow inside a pipeline?
options: The Data Flow activity
The Copy activity
The Lookup activity
Mapping data flows can't be run from a pipeline at all
questions.explain: A Data Flow activity operationalizes a mapping data flow inside a pipeline — parameterizable and chainable exactly like any other activity from Chapters 3 and 4.

questions.q: What does it mean when the Inspect tab shows nothing for a source?
options: The source has no defined schema — a schema-drift scenario with no fixed shape to describe yet
The data flow has a syntax error
Debug mode needs to be turned on first
The source transformation was deleted
questions.explain: Without a defined schema, there's genuinely no fixed column shape for Inspect to display — this is expected in schema-drift scenarios, not an error.
